summary: 64 de entries from Sami's spine and sourced supplemental seeds, built for per-platform route research.

entries.title: 64 de Hakken!! Tamagotchi Minna de Tamagotchi World

emulation.notes: Use accurate N64 emulation and preserve 4:3 presentation unless a verified widescreen route is tested. Japanese-only text/content should be expected.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: High-accuracy N64 emulation with clean digital capture

primary.version: Original Japanese Nintendo 64 release via high-accuracy N64 emulation
primary.why: There is a December 19, 1997 Nintendo 64 release and no other platform release. Because there is no PC/remaster path, the archive route is the original Japanese N64 version captured through a high-accuracy emulator for the cleanest image and stable capture.
primary.how_to_play: Use a legally dumped Japanese N64 cartridge image in a high-accuracy N64 emulator such as ares or simple64/Parallel-RDP. Capture at native 4:3 unless a tested widescreen hack is verified; keep the original Japanese release as the content authority.

all_releases.fidelity: Only sourced release; best archive fidelity comes from accurate N64 emulation and clean 4:3 capture rather than a nonexistent remaster.
all_releases.reason: primary: public release references and other platform references list Nintendo 64 as the release platform; no alternate platform or exclusive-content split is sourced.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced alternate release exists, so there is no fidelity-versus-completeness split to resolve.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced remaster, port, or localized release was found in this pass; revisit only if a later official release appears.

entries.title: Tamagotchi

emulation.notes: Capture physical hardware. Software recreations should be treated as separate preservation notes unless sourced as official equivalents.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Direct camera capture of original or official rerelease LCD hardware

primary.version: Generation 1 / Generation 2 original or official Original Tamagotchi rerelease
primary.why: The original Tamagotchi is a handheld virtual pet/electronic game, first released in Japan in 1996 and worldwide in 1997. Bandai's current Original Tamagotchi page says the rerelease uses the same programming as 1997, making current official hardware the practical route while vintage hardware remains the historical reference.
primary.how_to_play: Use an original or official Original Tamagotchi Gen 1/Gen 2 device, filmed directly with stable lighting. For historical capture, prefer a vintage unit; for practical play, the current Original Tamagotchi rerelease is acceptable if the goal is the 1997 programming loop.

all_releases.fidelity: Original monochrome LCD virtual-pet hardware with three-button interface and real-time care loop.
all_releases.reason: primary: content authority and historically exact route.

all_releases.fidelity: Modern official shell/reissue route using the same 1997 programming.
all_releases.reason: primary: practical current-hardware route for the original programming loop when vintage hardware is not required.

all_releases.platform: Later Tamagotchi toys and video game adaptations
all_releases.fidelity: Later devices and console/handheld games introduce different mechanics and should be treated as separate entries when needed.
all_releases.reason: skip: not alternate versions of the original 1996/1997 virtual pet loop.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Vintage hardware is historically exact; current Original Tamagotchi hardware is easier to source and uses the same 1997 programming. Choose based on whether the archive session values exact shell/history or practical play.

entries.remaster_caveats: Later Connection, color, Pix, Uni, and console/handheld video games are different Tamagotchi products rather than remasters of the original pet. Document the shell/model being used.
